id: title:eli-r-ph:count a null version as 0 in the version floor rpcs

review.posthog_relevance: Person identity replication consistency and recovery behavior
review.reason: Adds COALESCE(version, 0) to PostgreSQL UPDATE statements and clarifies comments; adds tests for NULL and zero version cases.
review.uncertainty: While the code change is substantive and bounded, the complete absence of the full PostgreSQL migration or replication configuration context prevents verification of whether this is a complete, tested recovery path or a partial patch. The tier is assigned based on the visible implementation and test additions, not on unverified production outcomes.

observations.limitations: This chunk is a single, cohesive change group. No unrelated PRs detected. No score assigned.

observations.behavior: Adds COALESCE(version, 0) to PostgreSQL UPDATE statements and clarifies comments; adds tests for NULL and zero version cases.
observations.code_quote: // Never lowers a version. A NULL version counts as 0, as in every other personhog write.
observations.posthog_connection: The person identity replication layer uses version numbers to guard against lowering a person's version. This patch ensures that a NULL version is treated as 0, preventing unintended version increases when the stored value is NULL, and explicitly documents this behavior.
